    Direct Thickness Model¶

    This notebook will use the spectranorm python package to fit a normative model for cortical thickness. The structure of this direct model will also be used (in later notebooks) to fit spectral normative models.

    class MyNumpyEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, np.integer):
            return int(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.floating):
            return float(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
            return obj.tolist()
        else:
            return super(MyEncoder, self).default(obj)


def ensure_dir(file_name):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_name), exist_ok=True)
    return file_name


def list_dirs(path=os.getcwd()):
    files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, '*'))
    files = [x for x in files if os.path.isdir(x)]
    return files


def file_exists(file_name, path_name=os.getcwd()):
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path_name, file_name))


def write_json(json_obj, file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'w') as outfile:
        json.dump(json_obj, outfile, sort_keys=True, indent=4,
                  cls=MyNumpyEncoder)
    return json_obj


def load_json(file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'r') as infile:
        return json.load(infile)


def write_np(np_obj, file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'wb') as outfile:
        np.save(outfile, np_obj)

    Copied! 
    # A nonlinear age effect modeled by a b-spline
age_min = 3                                # lowest_acceptable_age
age_max = 97                               # highest_acceptable_age
age_covariate = snm.CovariateSpec(
    name="age",                            # Column name as in the train/test dataframe
    cov_type="numerical",
    effect="spline",
    spline_spec=snm.SplineSpec(
        lower_bound=age_min,
        upper_bound=age_max,
        df=5, degree=3,
    )
)
ages = np.linspace(age_min, age_max, 200)
plt.plot(np.linspace(age_min, age_max, 200), age_covariate.make_spline_bases(ages));
age_covariate
    # A nonlinear age effect modeled by a b-spline age_min = 3 # lowest_acceptable_age age_max = 97 # highest_acceptable_age age_covariate = snm.CovariateSpec( name="age", # Column name as in the train/test dataframe cov_type="numerical", effect="spline", spline_spec=snm.SplineSpec( lower_bound=age_min, upper_bound=age_max, df=5, degree=3, ) ) ages = np.linspace(age_min, age_max, 200) plt.plot(np.linspace(age_min, age_max, 200), age_covariate.make_spline_bases(ages)); age_covariate

    # A categorical effect for sex
sex_covariate = snm.CovariateSpec(
    name="sex",                            # Column name as in the train/test dataframe
    cov_type="categorical",
    hierarchical=False,
    categories=demography_df['sex'].unique(),
)
sex_covariate
    # A categorical effect for sex sex_covariate = snm.CovariateSpec( name="sex", # Column name as in the train/test dataframe cov_type="categorical", hierarchical=False, categories=demography_df['sex'].unique(), ) sex_covariate 
    CovariateSpec(name=sex, cov_type=categorical, hierarchical=False, n_categories=2)

site_covariate = snm.CovariateSpec(
    name="site",                            # Column name as in the train/test dataframe
    cov_type="categorical",
    hierarchical=True,
    categories=demography_df['site'].unique(),
)
site_covariate

    Model Specification¶

    Copied! 
    normative_model = snm.DirectNormativeModel(
    spec=snm.NormativeModelSpec(
        variable_of_interest="thickness",
        covariates=[age_covariate, sex_covariate, site_covariate],
        influencing_mean=["age", "sex", "site"],
        influencing_variance=["age", "sex", "site"],
    ),
)
normative_model
    normative_model = snm.DirectNormativeModel( spec=snm.NormativeModelSpec( variable_of_interest="thickness", covariates=[age_covariate, sex_covariate, site_covariate], influencing_mean=["age", "sex", "site"], influencing_variance=["age", "sex", "site"], ), ) normative_model 
    DirectNormativeModel(spec=NormativeModelSpec(variable_of_interest='thickness', covariates=[CovariateSpec(name=age, cov_type=numerical, effect=spline), CovariateSpec(name=sex, cov_type=categorical, hierarchical=False, n_categories=2), CovariateSpec(name=site, cov_type=categorical, hierarchical=True, n_categories=189)], influencing_mean=['age', 'sex', 'site'], influencing_variance=['age', 'sex', 'site']))

    Model Visualization¶
    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    


    
Copied!


    
    

    

    %%time

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(12, 8))

age = demography_df['age']
xi = np.linspace(3, 97, 200)

# create dummy dataframe for prediction
test_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "age": xi,
})

# predict moments
moments = normative_model.predict(test_df, predict_without=['site', 'sex']).predictions

y_ppc_mu_mean = moments['mu_estimate']
y_ppc_sigma_mean = moments['std_estimate']

# need to ensure the correctness
quantiles = [0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95, 0.99, 0.999]

thickness_quantiles = {
    q: (
        (
            y_ppc_mu_mean + stats.norm.ppf(q=q) * (y_ppc_sigma_mean)
        )
    ) for q in quantiles
}

# colors for the plot
c1 = '#448e9c'  # brighter shade
c2 = '#038da6'  # darker shade

# centile plot
for q1, q2, alpha in [(0.001, 0.999, 0.05), (0.01, 0.99, 0.1), (0.05, 0.95, 0.2), (0.25, 0.75, 0.3)]:
    ax.fill_between(
        xi,
        thickness_quantiles[q1],
        thickness_quantiles[q2],
        alpha=alpha,
        color=c1,
    )
    
    # Now add boundary lines with different colors
    ax.plot(xi, thickness_quantiles[q1], color=c1, lw=0.5, linestyle=":",)
    ax.plot(xi, thickness_quantiles[q2], color=c1, lw=0.5, linestyle=":",)

ax.plot(
    xi,
    thickness_quantiles[0.5],
    c=c2,
    lw=4,
)

# logarithmic x-axis
# ax.set_xscale('log')

ax.set_xlim(3.5,96.5)

# Move legend outside
legend = ax.legend(
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),    # x=1.05 pushes it outside the axes
    loc='upper left',            # anchor point for placement
    borderaxespad=0.,            # padding
    fontsize=15,                 # font size
    markerscale=3,               # scale up legend markers (3x bigger than in the plot)
)

test_df = demography_df[demography_df["split"] == "Test"].copy()
test_df['harmonized_thickness'] = normative_model.harmonize(
    data=test_df, covariates_to_harmonize=['site'],
)

sns.scatterplot(
    data=test_df,
    x='age',
    y='harmonized_thickness',
    ax=ax,
    linewidth=0,
    hue='sex',
    palette="colorblind",
    alpha = 0.5,
    s=10,
    zorder=-20,
)

    # a path to save this sample direct model
save_path = "/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/data/pretrained_models/sample_direct_model/"

# first remove any older saved models
if Path(save_path).exists():
    shutil.rmtree(save_path)

# create the parent directory
Path(save_path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# save this model for later use
normative_model.save_model(Path(save_path))
